text: Wish you a happy New Year! May you turn a new leaf and become a valuable, positive, happy, tranquil and energetic human being – stand proud as the great warrior of truth and happiness, ready to strike down anything that is negative, anything that is not positive!!
author: Sri M

text: The secret of implementing a resolution is as the great Kabir Das said many hundred years ago:' kal karey so aaj kar, aaj karey so ab …', which means 'What you are supposed to do tomorrow, do it today; and what you need to do today, do it right now!' There is no other way. Postponement always ends in failure.
author: Sri M

text: Choose your goal carefully. Do that this New Year – may you have all success! Choose your goal – don’t have too many goals – three or four goals do not work. Have one goal and stick to it.
author: Sri M

text: The resolution has to be specific. If you resolve to be happy, have happiness as your aim – and, get ready to sacrifice everything else for happiness. Happiness is not attained by acquiring and gathering. It is attained by being good and ‘Letting Go!’ There is a great saying in the Ishavasya Upanishad – ‘ tyena tyaktena bhunjita ’ meaning, Let go and rejoice!
author: Sri M

text: ‘Let go’ doesn’t mean – give up. Throw everything and run away to the cave! That’s not what it means! Let go of all the unpleasant memories, the hurts, the wounds, the bitterness that's in your mind – let it all go.
author: Sri M

text: Let go and rejoice – let none of your hurts and negativities stick to you. Throw them away – let go of them. Then, be free and rejoice in the bliss of the tranquil mind which is at the core of your being. That’s the secret of happiness!
author: Sri M

text: Write down your goal – WRITE IT DOWN. Every night, before you go to sleep, take the slip, read it as many times as you can. Repeat it like a mantra. Put it under your pillow and go to sleep. Believe me, if you are serious and sacrifice your time and energy, the mind will find ways and means to bring about situations that will open up your future to fulfilling the aim. This is true, as imagination is a gift from the Divine.
author: Sri M

text: Patanjali in the Yoga Sutras, while discussing the question - How does one make the mind one-pointed, free from agitation, says there is only one way. There are no short cuts. Nirantara deergha kaala abhyasena, meaning ‘Practice, practice, practice for a long, long time’ – this is the only way to implement your resolutions; to clear up your mind; to make it positive and free it from negativity.
author: Sri M

text: A small good deed, a kind deed done to another human being or another living creature, can wipe out the dirt of negativity that has gathered in your soul and make it free and clear as a mirror to reflect Divinity.
author: Sri M

text: So, let this be our resolution this year. That we will resolve to do the best we can to help at least one unfortunate human being. And two, we shall let go of all negativities, of all hatred and anger in us from last year and rejoice in the goodness and happiness, peace and brotherhood of the whole world.
author: Sri M

text: I am not denying you might need some help from a teacher on a journey of such large uncharted territory, this search for Truth; but the moment the teacher becomes more important than the teaching, you are in trouble.
author: Sri M

text: The whole search for Truth should start with understanding our relationship with nature and how we relate to other human beings, or even animals. It’s not something isolated, we are part of one big whole.
author: Sri M

text: True freedom emerges when the mind is absolutely at rest - at peace with itself and the world. Not grasping, not in conflict, not reaching out, not stretching itself but remaining in its original state of calm and completeness. This state is called moksha or freedom.
author: Sri M

text: In the state of moksha or freedom, the human mind, even the physical body, undergoes a certain change. The cells change, the psyche changes, everything changes. The person becomes a entirely new individual, resting in an innate freedom. That is Moksha.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is settled, there are no distractions; it's at peace. If it’s at peace with itself, then it is at peace with the world outside. The aim of yoga is to bring the rush of thoughts to a peaceful quietness.
author: Sri M

text: The purpose of spiritual training is to become one-pointed, and then to finally let go. The Upanishad says - 'Tena tyaktena bhunjitha', meaning 'let go and rejoice!
author: Sri M

text: Om Namah Shivaya - I bow down to that supreme Shiva who encompasses all the levels of consciousness, from waking state to the dream state and beyond into turiya. I bow down to Shivam for the Truth to be illumined and awakened in my heart.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is any attempt to make your mind quiet and move beyond your ordinary limitations. Bhakti Yoga, Jnana Yoga, Karma Yoga - all these are different modes of journey to the Truth, depending on the individual.
author: Sri M

text: Samadhi - the state when the person is so absorbed in meditation that there is no distinction between the meditator and the thing meditated upon. Everything becomes one and there is absolutely no distraction, it is still and quiet. When what remains is 'That' and nothing else, even I forget that I'm there. This is Samadhi.
author: Sri M

text: The Gita defines Yoga as ‘ Yogam karmasu kausalya’ - Yoga is to work with complete tranquility and auspiciousness. The Yogasutras of Patanjali, considered by many as the standard textbook, starts by defining Yoga not as an Asana or Pranayama but as ‘ Yoganushasanam ’. Here begins the teaching on Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The Hatha Yoga Pradipika says the Asanas and Pranayama are the stepping stones. Asana, according to Patanjali, is defined in one sentence: ‘ Sthira sukham Asanam’ . The posture giving you comfort for a length of time is your Asana.
author: Sri M

text: Moderation is essential, especially in practicing Yoga Asanas . Asanas are not just physical exercise; they don't focus on muscle building. Of course, they keep your muscles fit and supple. They hold your spine steady.
author: Sri M

text: We never give attention to our breath, despite its importance. If it stops, we are dead. Give attention and we can see it start to slow down. After a while,we feel like letting out a deep sigh!. We are then settled. Pranayama is the science of calming our Prana using our breath.
author: Sri M

text: The Yogis of ancient times wondered:If the condition of the mind is affecting one's breath, is it possible to change the breathing rhythm so that the mind can be pacified? From this insight, many pranayamas came to be. A simple evidence - if you watch your breath or become aware of your breath, the breath slows down.
author: Sri M

text: Pratyahara is the capacity the Yogi has to develop by fixing his attention one-pointedly. He should be able to do this at will. If one is able to fix attention and not able to withdraw it, then one is obsession. But a yogi is not an obsessed person; he can fix his attention and withdraw it at will. It comes only through practice.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is the practical way of living in this world, yet moving forward through the mind. This one-pointedness comes through practice - fixing and withdrawing attention. As Patanjali has said, ‘ Nairantarya abhyase’ , it comes only through regular and incessant practice. There are no shortcuts.
author: Sri M

text: With the limited framework we call rationalism, we cannot find the Infinite. Yes, we can approach it theoretically. You cross the threshold only when you realize with complete humility that you can't find the Infinite with the rational mind. If you could, it wouldn’t be Infinite anymore. What emerges from this understanding is humility, which is close to Bhakti, 'devotion'.
author: Sri M

text: For self-realization, one must first understand the limitations of oneself - physically, emotionally, spiritually, psychologically - before being able to break through. If I don’t know where I stand, how will I take a step forward?
author: Sri M

text: In the ordinary, material world, if one can suspend the limiting thought and say,"this is only creating problems for me, let me set it aside", one will see ways open up! Although we are limited, there is a potential within us for the unlimited. This is possible at all levels - physical, psychological, and spiritual.
author: Sri M

text: Does one become the Brahman simply by saying I am the Brahman ? It necessitates an extraordinary change of mind and a certain rebooting of the brain. This rebooting has to occur through Yoga. By Yoga, I don't mean Hatha yoga but Yoga in the sense of a movement to the core.
author: Sri M

text: As far as the spiritual progress is concerned, you cannot leave your brain in cold storage, shut it up, and say, "Now, I am spiritual". There is much more toit. Spiritual life is about coming to terms with reality - where we are, what we are doing, how we are moving, and so on.
author: Sri M

text: The earliest verse of the Rig Veda talks about creation and says - 'perhaps he knows or perhaps he knows not'. Each one of us, with our limitations, needs to understand what we are, how we are related to this world, and how - while still in this world -we will be able to free ourselves from it.
author: Sri M

text: The student or the listener must realize there are things to be learnt, of which he knows little and say: ‘Let me listen to somebody who seems to know’. This attitude curtails the egotistic feeling that comes in between when we listen.
author: Sri M

text: The whole search for Truth should start with understanding our relationship with nature and how we relate to other human beings, or even animals. It’s not something isolated, we are part of one big whole.
author: Sri M

text: When you go to a cave, you don't go alone. You take your mind with you. There are two fellows there, you and your mind, constantly tussling within the cave. When that incessant tussle stops and there is no conflict left, you begin to discover there is a mind, other than the brain, that keeps bothering you all the time. But this must be discovered.
author: Sri M

text: This completeness that we are seeking - which the Upanishad says and many people have found - can't be found outside of one's self. When the mind becomes quiet and settles down having understood that satisfaction cannot be found anywhere else and that completeness we are seeking can be found in this completeness here. This is the search we are on.
author: Sri M

text: When the beauty of our true essence is seen within, then everything is complete. This is what we seek, but unfortunately, it's impossible to understand with one's normal state of mind. Yes, there are techniques to make the mind more sensitive to grasp this understanding. The process of Sadhana is to connect to that part of our minds with which we can touch the Infinite.
author: Sri M

text: When they say ' Maya ', what they mean is that it is not permanent. Please make a distinction between permanent and not existing. The whole theory of illusion means what you think will exist forever and is real, may not exist after ten minutes. Therefore it's not real. But while it exists, it's very real.
author: Sri M

text: When we usually say S amadhi , we mean 'Savikalpa samadhi' where there are no vikalpas - where everything is quiet. The next stage of Samadhi is ' Nirvikalpa ', where there's nothing left. Beyond that is 'Sahaja' , where you are in your true state all the time, where you are not going in or coming out, where nothing is happening, and everything is the same.
author: Sri M

text: Many hundred years ago, the great Kabir Das divulged the secret of implementing a resolution: 'kal karey so aaj kar, aaj karey so ab…', meaning 'What you are supposed to do tomorrow, do it today; and what you need to do today, do it now!' Postponing things always ends in failure.
author: Sri M

text: Kabir Das narrates the story of the Kasturi Mriga (Musk Deer), an apt illustration of the human predicament. The poor deer wanders all over, trying to locate the source of the fragrance emanating from its own body. The Kasturi , the treasure is right within us. Where are we searching? Just turn inwards!
author: Sri M

text: ‘Ja ghat prem na sanchare, so ghat jaan masan (smashaan). Jaise khal Lohar ki Saans let bin praan’. The iron monger’s bellows also breathe, but if there’s no love in one’s heart, there’s no point.
author: Sri M

text: If I say I know everything, then there is no movement, research, or inquiry. It is what we don’t know that inspires us to seek and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: We can’t live on our past heritage alone; we must look at the now. The entire spiritual movement, scientific progress, is based on the understanding that ‘I don’t know’.
author: Sri M

text: If we start our spiritual journey saying ’I know’, then one doesn’t get to know anything.
author: Sri M

text: If we are looking for something infinite that cannot be captured in words and cannot be defined, then we are starting from ‘I don’t know’.
author: Sri M

text: Can there be knowledge of that which ‘Is’? When we try to understand this with our conditioned brain, we gain the insight that all things one gathers in one’s head are a memory. And if it is a memory, it is something in the past, and if it is something in the past, it cannot be the reality that is always the present.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishads say that the Truth is something which is far and yet so near; it moves but it’s faster than any movement, it’s that which is, and not that which was. Every minute, it is new.
author: Sri M

text: Only when the mind has ceased all finding, grasping, and then settled down in that silence, something happens.
author: Sri M

text: These layers of prejudice close the eyes, ears, and heart. When the wind blows, nothing can enter. So, all the practices we do are meant to open the windows.
author: Sri M

text: Surrender means to understand that I am helpless at a certain point and, therefore, I need to relax, let go, be patient and wait. In that waiting, something arrives. The breeze may be from within.
author: Sri M

text: Ultimately, you are your own Master. There is no other. A teacher can help you understand this point. If you do, then you are free. My job is to tell you that your teacher is in you.
author: Sri M

text: Nobody can give us illumination; we have to find it ourselves. Just as one who is hungry has to find food for oneself.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot have a healthy body without a healthy mind. One of the prerequisites of a healthy body is to eat less, and do good exercise.
author: Sri M

text: In India, the wandering teacher is called a Parivrajaka - one who continuously walks in search of the truth. Once the truth is found, the teacher must take it door-to-door.
author: Sri M

text: We carry so many things in our head. Be simple. Throw off the burdens and be free!
author: Sri M

text: A mind that has no distractions can have effortless one-pointed attention. When the eye of intuition or the eye of one-pointedness opens, then you can see the light.
author: Sri M

text: Any place, where the truth is worshipped, is a temple for us. The most important temple is the body. Inside us is the heart where the Truth sits.
author: Sri M

text: If you are on the spiritual path, if you are moving towards the Truth, the first steps are - try to be truthful in day-to-day life. You cannot tell lies 24 hours a day and expect to find the Absolute Truth.
author: Sri M

text: No matter what happens, don’t bother. You may suffer reverses, and you may get into trouble. Stick to your spiritual path, if you are serious.
author: Sri M

text: When you find a spiritual teacher after a few years of observation, one who you think is worth it, ask for the real thing. Don’t ask for the petty stuff. Sometimes in trouble, one asks for such things, it’s okay. However, always keep in mind that what you have to look for is That.
author: Sri M

text: People think that to be spiritual means to start healing. First, you have to heal yourself. ‘Physician, heal thyself’. Heal your spirit first; there are enough hospitals and doctors to heal the sick. And, the way to heal yourself is to look for your true self, your communication with the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: The worship of the teacher shouldn't take so much precedence that the teaching is forgotten.
author: Sri M

text: What is spirituality? It is to find the truth, to find yourself, to find who you are, and what your link with Supreme Being is. This is the primary goal of spiritual practice. If you are with a spiritual teacher, this is precisely what he or she will like to inculcate in you.
author: Sri M

text: When a spiritual teacher is blunt, he is doing his duty of guiding or shocking people out of their illusions. Already, were in illusion. Now, why create more illusions besides this?
author: Sri M

text: When you sit for long periods before a Dhuni and meditate, it is about you contemplating on the outer fire - an act that helps to light the inner fire.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest miracle is having the ability to lead a person to spiritual growth. Beyond that, there is no bigger miracle, and it is the most challenging miracle possible.
author: Sri M

text: The idea of the teacher should be to make you self-reliant. If a teacher makes you totally dependent, then there are either two reasons for that: one, he wants you to be always dependent on him, and the other is he is probably dependent on you.
author: Sri M

text: For most people, the greatest miracle is to bring about a transformation in thinking. The change in thinking is to turn inward and try to figure out what life is all about. Figuring out what our link with life is, what is life itself, whether I am just here to be born and die, or is there something more than this.
author: Sri M

text: There is a divinity in every heart, and that divinity - by its very essence - is peace, tranquility, and happiness. The more you tune into it, the happier you are, the better your mind is, and the better you function in your relationship with others.
author: Sri M

text: The mind has to be kept lively, no matter the consequences - including physical age. There are ways and means to achieve this. One is to decide that you are not going to let yourself feel old within. That's the first step, and then you have to start working it out point-by-point. First, look at life with an open mind; be vigilant, be agile.
author: Sri M

text: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna tells Arjuna that the mind can be a friend, but the same mind can also be an enemy. Cultivate the friendly side of your mind. And, don’t give too much attention to the enemy.
author: Sri M

text: When you are alone, that's the only time you are really with yourself. Then, you get to see your mind and how you relate to other people. These are amazing levels of consciousness you can be aware of when you are alone.
author: Sri M

text: Being alone actually means experiencing the feeling of all being one. I like to speak that word – alone. All one. It’s like the whole universe is part of you when you are alone.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t be afraid of being left alone. It’s beautiful, that’s the time when you talk to yourself. That’s also when you talk to your God. When left alone, that's the time you are allowed to look into yourself and find out where your problems are. So, appreciate it when you are alone and be thankful to those who have let you be alone.
author: Sri M

text: Sharing is an essential part of well-being. As you give, so you receive. So, give whenever possible, whatever possible, in whichever way you can.
author: Sri M

text: We end up usually with an image or outcome of our expectation. When the real thing arrives, we cannot or do not recognize it. The only way to find the Truth is to take the images or expectations out of our minds.
author: Sri M

text: In the spiritual sphere, we miss the obvious because we desire for the exotic. Spirituality is a beautiful breeze, moving grass, tranquil mountains, sitting quietly and hearing the church bells toll. This is spirituality in essence and once one settles down, you will find that it also happens within.
author: Sri M

text: What you seek is right within you, but we search for it everywhere but in us. Inside us, there is a beautiful treasure which we tend to miss.
author: Sri M

text: We have forgotten to sit under trees. In ancient times, all the teachers sat under the tree and taught. The Buddha got his enlightenment under a peepal tree.
author: Sri M

text: The importance of a pilgrimage is in the act of walking. You are walking together in a group. Rig Veda says: May we walk together, may we study together, with our minds put together, may we understand!
author: Sri M

text: In a pilgrimage when people come together, there is always a sharing and an emergence of our inner workings – we get to see the beginning of what we actually are
author: Sri M

text: Knowing oneself starts with knowing oneself in the midst of people, not alone. In seclusion, I don’t see how I am. We should first know who we are and where we stand. To know thyself means knowing myself as I am, instead of just repeating ‘I am the Brahman’! I can’t be angry, jealous, narrow and still be Brahman.
author: Sri M

text: If we are making spiritual progress, don’t judge by how many visions or kind of lights one sees. What we have to look at is how one behaves. Have I become less selfish? Has my world narrowed down or has it expanded? Do I feel bad for the child next door or is it only for my child?
author: Sri M

text: The main idea is to watch ourselves diligently in our dealings with the world and see if we are changing, turning more human. We cannot run away from the world, right? So, the first thing is to see how I behave. Am I really free? It’s not easy to be free of anger, for example.
author: Sri M

text: Peace is a state of mind that emerges from within. If I am not peaceful with myself, then I cannot bring peace anywhere. Why? Because there is conflict in our minds always. We are constantly pulled in multiple directions, and the mind has no rest.
author: Sri M

text: If we have one mind, a change in one part should affect the other. So, if we change ourselves, that change will affect all.
author: Sri M

text: What happens in solitude? We are face-to-face with ourselves, where one sits for long hours and does absolutely nothing. For example - sit and look at the lake. The closer we are to trees and nature, and further we are from human-made things, one’s mind can settle down more effortlessly.
author: Sri M

text: Once one is established in this silence, then no noise can disturb you. Silence is not the absence of sound. As long as the chatter of the mind remains, there is no solitude. In the depths of your heart, there is silence. You sometimes come upon it when you look at the lake or the mountain. Why we don’t come upon it is because we compare and judge, whereby the chattering starts.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual life is not merely sitting down and enjoying as if you were having a drink in the bar. Spiritual growth is coming to terms with reality, having an awareness of where we are, what we are doing, etc.
author: Sri M

text: Each one of us, with our limitations, needs to understand the fact of how we are related to this world, and how, while we are still in this world, can free ourselves from it.
author: Sri M

text: If your search for the Truth is serious, then the right kind of guidance will come in some way. You have to remain sincere.
author: Sri M

text: While personal understanding and guidance are essential, it is also important that one’s aspiration for spiritual knowledge is profound.
author: Sri M

text: If you are seeking a spiritual teacher, get rid of the conventional ideas you may have about a teacher, because that prejudice may prevent you from seeing a real teacher.
author: Sri M

text: Mantras have a built-in vibration. Even if you don’t understand them, they have an impact. Sanskrit is such a language. When one chants it, the mind and the breath get into a rhythm. This will organize the mind’s waves into a specific order.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t just accept what someone says. The idea is to go within oneself. If one doesn’t go into one’s mind, one cannot comprehend the different layers of the mind, which generally creates all our problems.
author: Sri M

text: For identifying the different layers, no one can give you a ready-made formula. I cannot say ‘you are like this, you are like that’. How you are, only you know. And you have to find out. What a teacher helps with is showing a way of looking at it.
author: Sri M

text: In general, we don’t look at ourselves, and we blame others because we are either not prepared or we don’t have the guts to open ourselves up to take a look. We are afraid we might be opening a ‘Pandora’s Box’.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishads are here to help us find our true self. Find out for yourself. It’s the process of going deeper and deeper into one’s inner layers of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: In the process of delving into the mind, there is a lot of churning. When you churn, just like the ancient ‘ Samudra Manthan’ (churning of the ocean), the first thing that emerges is poison. Unfortunately for us, there is no Shiva around to consume it. This poison must appear first and, then only will the Amrit (nectar) come.
author: Sri M

text: Churning is the process of looking within. Looking within is not just sitting with one’s eyes closed. Churning means to watch your mind, to be watchful of your interactions in your everyday life towards your near and dear and the others. That's when you realise who and what you are.
author: Sri M

text: When emotions come, don’t run away from them. Feel what is happening. Being emotional human beings, we cannot discover ourselves in a ‘dry’ emotionless manner. Only when we experience emotions are we human beings. That's when we can look at ourselves to learn and understand who we are.
author: Sri M

text: What you discover, sans your emotions, is merely a false image of yourself, it’s not you. It’s an emotion-free imitation that's not real. We are full of emotions. Always, keep that channel open.
author: Sri M

text: Sat Chit Ananda! Sat is the reality of everything. Chit is consciousness by which you experience, feel or realize the reality. Ananda is bliss or happiness. Since it's difficult to directly touch Sat (absolute reality of what is) and fully comprehend Chit , the only way is through Bhakti or Ananda . When true Ananda is recognised, Chit and Sat are automatically understood.
author: Sri M

text: How does a person grow? Not by owning huge properties and great wealth but by beginning to think that everyone is important and essential.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest penance is to calmly and quietly hear someone insulting us with absolutely no reaction. And, at the end of it, to say ‘thank you very much’. That would be the highest penance for a yogi.
author: Sri M

text: It’s a burden to carry unnecessary material in your head, especially if you are seeking something new, something which is fresh. It is better to keep it all out. You don’t need to use your mind to find new things, now-a-days.
author: Sri M

text: The ancient seekers said, it’s true, you are looking for happiness, completeness and fulfillment. However, as you have not found it outside, have you even considered that perhaps, you can find it inside?
author: Sri M

text: The breath is the link to the inner consciousness. Therefore the first step is to turn your mind and engage it in your breathing patterns.
author: Sri M

text: To be spiritual is not to shut off your brain. People afraid of being exposed might say ‘Hey, don’t think, just accept it’, I don’t say that. Think, find out for yourself! When you find out for yourself, it’s your understanding, not mine. If you only accept what I’m saying, it’s second-hand.
author: Sri M

text: What is sought outside can be found within. And what you find here is complete. Once you touch That, and understand the joy of the fountainhead from which happiness arises, you lead a satisfied and happy life. Then, there is an incessant urge to share it - that makes you work.
author: Sri M

text: There is a two-pronged journey towards the discovery of the truth. One, try to find out through a systematic inquiry how the brain reacts, where is the pineal gland, and how does it work? The other, is through one’s own direct experience.
author: Sri M

text: Through yoga - using the mind - one can activate these centers in the brain which have been dead for centuries. When the centers are activated, the whole world expands and one perceives a larger expanse. You obtain a universal outlook, you think differently.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya is one of the ways of yoga in which it’s understood that the state of one’s mind can be altered through varying the rhythm of your breathing.
author: Sri M

text: Think outside the box. Don’t go solely based on linear logic; use fuzzy logic. Turn things upside down and look, you will see things are quite different.
author: Sri M

text: The mindset should be unprejudiced. Only then does inquiry start.
author: Sri M

text: Look at the Upanishads; nobody preaches anything there. They say - ‘Explore’!
author: Sri M

text: On your spiritual quest, it’s not necessary to get detached from social relationships completely. That’s not required. In fact, it’s only while living in this world with others that one can discover what you are, who you are and where you stand.
author: Sri M

text: Isn’t it better to alter the mind with breathing than by taking a chemical substance? Kriya yoga is taught to alter the mind without taking ‘bhang’. Chemical substances have repercussions, and the brain becomes dull afterwards. But here, the brain becomes active, sharp, and perhaps goes beyond what you can achieve with a drug.
author: Sri M

text: To ‘empty oneself’ sounds simple. However, it's the most difficult thing because we are so full of our thoughts, our prejudices and what others have taught us. There is no space; we are filled to the brim.
author: Sri M

text: How can one learn when one is full? Empty all the things we instantly like or dislike since our subconsciousness is conditioned to certain things. Essentially, to empty all this is the process of sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: When I say I have to empty myself, it implies I am already full. All this has to be examined, and unless and until a vessel is empty, it cannot be filled. Here, the vessel is the mind or brain, so full of the prejudices built up along life's journey.
author: Sri M

text: Emptying oneself is neither a conscious nor an unconscious process. We need to understand it as a concept. There is no technique to do this. The concept should be there in one’s mind constantly so that while living in this world and interacting with others, the process of emptying commences. So, in the every-day life, can we meet and interact with people without prejudices?
author: Sri M

text: If somebody has indeed emptied his or her mind in the process of life, there is a stillness that arises when the mind is without distraction.
author: Sri M

text: When we meditate, we see that the mind wanders - either because we are attracted to something or repulsed by something. If this unrest is settled by the understanding that this is the cause of one not being empty and free, then it becomes easier to sit and meditate.
author: Sri M

text: Pranava is that which gives the first thrust to the life forces. It’s the Alpha and the Omega. In the ancient tradition, it is called Aum.
author: Sri M

text: Ved - means to study, Anta means the end. So, Ved-anta means understanding when the need to study ends. To reach a state, the Truth, which when understood there is no need to read or study to understand it.
author: Sri M

text: What is Upanishad? ‘Upa’- means to be near, ‘shad’ - means to sit. Not only are you physically sitting down, but your mind has also settled down. Another meaning is ‘to shake up’ all the theories we carry about the world and ourselves. When we study Vedanta, it shakes us out of our stupor. We live with so many ideas.
author: Sri M

text: There is a small word in between ‘Upa’ and ‘shad’ - ‘Ni’. ‘Ni’ indicates the position of one who teaches and one who's listening. The student sits with the attitude, ‘I don’t know, let me understand.’ It means listening as if one is hearing it for the first time. ‘Ni’ also means the receiving vessel is placed lower than the source of knowledge. And, it has to be empty. Space is required to imbibe knowledge.
author: Sri M

text: There are some who go for talks and spend all their time comparing. This fellow says this, and somebody else said that. When you are listening, you should listen to it fully and not compare. When you compare, half your mind is engaged in this. For the Upanishads, you need 100% of your energy because we are talking about very subtle thoughts.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes what happens is we read so much of the scriptures that there is not enough space within to accommodate the understanding.
author: Sri M

text: The Mandukya Upanishad says, ‘A’, the first sound in Aum represents the waking state that is common to all of us. You may believe in God, you may not, or you may be an agnostic. But everyone experiences the waking state - Jagrata. This is common to all living beings.
author: Sri M

text: The ‘U’ sound in Aum represents the dream state that is common to all humanity. This is called the ‘Swapna Avasta’ or the ‘Tejasa’ - that which is illumined or lit by itself. Why? Because when you are dreaming, you think it’s real.
author: Sri M

text: Yajnavalkya says to King Janaka, ‘When you were dreaming, there was a witness to the dream. When you were awake, there was a witness to the state of waking. So, the witness is the reality and not what it witnesses.’
author: Sri M

text: Sleep is so rejuvenating because one is fully unaware then that they exist. The moment one knows, there is no rest. That’s when all the issues crop up. ‘I’ am the first problem. The problem starts with ‘Me’.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind settles down quietly, when there are no ripples on its surface, perhaps then one identifies the witness that's watching everything.
author: Sri M

text: In the Yoga Sutras, there is Prakriti - primal matter, and Purusha – pure consciousness. The Purusha is the witness to all the activities of Prakriti.
author: Sri M

text: Turiya is a state where the witness remains without getting involved in the waking state, dream state and deep sleep. If it is possible in deep sleep to somehow wake up and be aware, that would be Turiya.
author: Sri M

text: Beyond the mind is Purusha – pure consciousness, which is the witness to all the activities of Prakriti. When the mind frees itself from the opposites of Prakriti and becomes quiet and non-dual, then the Purusha is reflected in its purity. In Yoga, this is called Kaivalya.
author: Sri M

text: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali say, ‘Yogas chitta vritti nirodha.’ The process of Yoga is to stop the continuous movement caused by the distractions of the mind-stuff. Practically, it’s Yoga; theoretically, it’s Vedanta because Yoga is a way to experience what's been described in the Vedanta.
author: Sri M

text: There was a time when the Vedantin thought one could attain Kaivalya merely by reflection and saying, ‘I am Brahman’. Yogic practice is the process by which we will experience it as a result of a clear mind.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not only physical exercises. That's just one aspect required to keep your body healthy. But, the most important part is meditation, also known as ‘dhyana’.
author: Sri M

text: Samadhi is the culmination of the practice of Yoga, where all the distractions of the mind-stuff are removed, and the mind becomes absolutely calm and quiet. In that quiet, ripple-less mind, is reflected the Purusha, the Self.
author: Sri M

text: When Purusha is experienced, the human being begins to understand that the fullness, completeness, security, and happiness we were seeking in the outside world are all found within. There is no better example of this than Turiya.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind becomes still and quiet, it turns within and comes to the Source. Such a person cannot be selfish. Why? One is selfish when one craves for something. What happens when you don’t want anything? Such a person only gives because that person has experienced ‘Poorna’, completeness.
author: Sri M

text: In Sankya, everything is ruled by the three gunas – Tamas, Rajas and Sattva. Simplified, these mean lethargy or darkness, energy for action and goodness respectively. Each person has a different ratio of these gunas within. The idea is to evolve from Tamas - lethargy towards Rajas - activity and, from there, move to Sattva, goodness.
author: Sri M

text: Very often, people mistake lethargy for Sattva because goodness is calm and tranquil. Somebody may say they are meditating, but actually they are sleeping.
author: Sri M

text: One day, you reach Sattva in its pure state. Then, you drop even that, and then there is Reality.
author: Sri M

text: No one can spiritually advance by simply sitting down cross-legged and meditating 24 hours. The moment you begin to see divinity in all living beings and start serving human beings, the mind can begin to purify and reach higher states. Service is an important part of Sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: By serving somebody, you are doing nothing actually. The person whom you serve is giving you an opportunity to evolve. ‘You’ are not giving anybody anything. If ‘you’ don’t, somebody else will provide. Nature’s law is that they will receive it somehow. We should have this in mind when we serve people.
author: Sri M

text: All beings are divinity in living form. Serving living beings is the best worship you can do. The more you help, the purer you become, and the clearer your mind becomes.
author: Sri M

text: Tamo guna through service, evolves to Sattva and the mind becomes purified. Not only do you progress upwards, but you also take along with you, those whom you have served. To me, service is a significant part of one’s spiritual life.
author: Sri M

text: There are some rules of life one should follow before starting the practice. For instance, can we live without injuring other living beings, even for food? Can we try to restrain ourselves as much as we can from outbursts of anger and jealousy? Now, while we work on these things, we should also start our inner practice. It’s possible to move forward this way.
author: Sri M

text: What we see in this world today is a result of the lopsided development of the frontal lobe. Due to this, so many other parts of the brain have been neglected. They lie latent and can be activated. It’s time now to evolve towards the spiritual.
author: Sri M

text: The idea is that every human being evolves and reaches perfection ultimately. Not that ready-made perfection can be gifted to somebody. I don’t think even Babaji can do that.
author: Sri M

text: Babaji has said that the difficult time humanity is going through is like the churning of the ocean - Samudra Manthan. Every soul exposed to this, will through experience go through it and emerge on the other side.
author: Sri M

text: Great teachers are always there to guide you through the turbulence of the churning yet not spoon-feed you. They know it is going to be the destiny of the world ultimately.
author: Sri M

text: Why not think of spiritual development as something where we need to put in a lot of work? As long as it remains a hobby, we make some progress but not go beyond. Nowadays, people meditate to be free from stress and lose weight! While that’s fine, the real trip begins only when we get serious and say, this is not what I’m looking for!
author: Sri M

text: I was looking for a simple and direct way to walk. My intention was to find the truth, and nothing but the truth. No fancy trimmings. It was not easy, but I managed.
author: Sri M

text: I decided, ‘I am walking on this path, it’s a lonely path’. Like Jesus Christ said, 'It’s a straight and narrow path’. So, let’s stick to it and not get sidetracked. This was always on my mind.
author: Sri M

text: It’s good to learn from various sources. Just make sure that you don’t get caught up in it because some people are always shopping. This shouldn’t happen in your spiritual search, as a form of spiritual consumerism or entertainment.
author: Sri M

text: One of the simple things people need to develop is single-pointed attention. This is useful in anything, material or spiritual, whichever way you choose to go in life.
author: Sri M

text: The problem is that throughout the day you are distracted; how can you expect the mind to be one-pointed when you meditate? So, whatever work you are doing, if you can give complete attention to that, you will also be able to do meditation with full attention.
author: Sri M

text: Breath is such an important part of our existence, but we don’t give it any attention. Just shift focus and observe it for 10 minutes a day with eyes closed. While inhaling, say ‘hum’, and while exhaling, say ‘so’ silently. When one begins to enjoy it, the mind becomes one-pointed. This has to be part of your daily life. It is practical and non-denominational.
author: Sri M

text: If a person understands that the divine exists in all living beings, no living beings would be afraid of him nor will he be afraid of any. This is an experience I had with Babaji when it came to snakes and bears. Nothing bothered him because he didn’t intend any harm to them. Animals realize this better than humans.
author: Sri M

text: We have to change first; we can’t change the world until we transform. Small drops make the ocean.
author: Sri M

text: We all have this disease wherein we believe we are isolated, insignificant individuals and are different from each other. When this misconception is removed, then only One remains. All become One.
author: Sri M

text: Questions never end. When you figure out that questions are part of the movement of the mind, and everything is still, there is nothing left to ask. This is something that has to happen on its own; it’s not something that can be imposed on anybody.
author: Sri M

text: Satsang is Sat-sang. ‘Sat’ means that which is true, that which always is. Amidst the movement of life, there is this essence that’s permanent. It was and is always there. It has no religion, no gender, and no political affiliation. It is there for everyone. ‘Sanga’ means a group of like-minded people coming together and trying to investigate this Truth.
author: Sri M

text: We believe there are as many ways to spiritual fulfillment as there are people. It cannot be the same for everyone because we are all made differently. So, your approach could be one of the ways, but when you reach the goal you will say, ‘Aha, they are all the same!’
author: Sri M

text: It’s the straight and narrow path. Start slow. Patience is very important. You should care for how you live. Spiritual practice is not that you continue to live how you live and practice in a mechanical way. You should also change your life. Then, if you bring a technique to it, you may move.
author: Sri M

text: In each individual’s spiritual journey, the speed may differ. There are many influences and reasons, so one should never give up. Carry on!
author: Sri M

text: This Truth that we seek, it’s almost like no-thing. Which is why the Buddha called it Shunya. When my ego becomes zero, then I see that zero. That Nothing is the essence of everything.
author: Sri M

text: Consciousness is complete. What we call energy is also consciousness. What we call physical or gross material also comes from this spiritual completeness. And, even if has taken many shapes and sizes, it’s all actually One. Even if subtracted, it remains full.
author: Sri M

text: Some great spiritual teachers are so absorbed in the fullness just like a full vessel. There is no sound; there’s no need to speak.
author: Sri M

text: Deep down, the preparation is to have space, to empty the prejudices, to be free. There needs to be space. The preparation can be done in any tradition.
author: Sri M

text: The wounds, hurts and hatred that we carry in our hearts; this is the biggest barrier to space. It’s muck. And if you don’t clean this muck, there is no space for it to happen. And when there is space, everything is within us.
author: Sri M

text: Sleep is like a mini-death. So, can we get up in the morning fresh and see, as if everything is new?
author: Sri M

text: There is this constant desire to be complete, to be full. This is how life moves, and we never seem to find this completeness outside. So, if it can be found inside, you will see it reflected outside.
author: Sri M

text: It is the experience of many, that completeness comes when our little selfish personality that is only thinking about me and myself has gone. Then I think only of ‘you, you’. Your pain becomes my pain. It’s no longer localized. Your happiness is my happiness. This is not theory or philosophy; it’s the experience of those who have touched that completeness.
author: Sri M

text: We have now come to a stage in the evolution of the average human mind, that we can find that truth right here living in a normal way, meaning wearing normal clothes, with a family, a job and so on. The days when you had to find the Truth by running off into a cave is over. We can evolve while we are here and now.
author: Sri M

text: When you interact with the world, that’s when you can really see where you stand.
author: Sri M

text: The paths are many, and the goal is total fullness and completeness. This is what we are all seeking though we may not be spiritually inclined. If even a few people understand this and start living this way, we can change the world.
author: Sri M

text: In the highest spiritual experience, you see that you are One. You are not different.
author: Sri M

text: To begin one’s spiritual journey, the starting mind must be a quiet mind, a tranquil mind. It is a runway from which you can take off.All spiritual practices are meant to bring about a tranquil and quiet mind.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest dharma is not to hurt or injure others, and cause no grief to others. Have affection towards everyone. This is the complete definition of dharma.When a person does his or her duty, they are already less selfish because they are doing it for others. When they grow more, everyone becomes their family.
author: Sri M

text: There are some qualities that we need to develop to lead a dharmic life. We need to know how to keep our senses under control. There has to be moderation. Remain tranquil at all times under all circumstances, whether someone is praising or insulting us. Can we maintain our equilibrium? And, have the welfare of all living beings in our heart?
author: Sri M

text: To be spiritual does not mean to become weak. Forgiveness is a great strength. It’s the weak that cannot forgive.
author: Sri M

text: In the ultimate essence, nobody can do anything to our true essence. If you are fixed there, then nothing matters. And, when you are full, the fullness flows, and you want to share it with others. The fullness is always auspicious. It is called Shivam.
author: Sri M

text: Shivam means consciousness, bliss, and auspiciousness. It is present within us and moving towards it is the spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: Oneness is so difficult to achieve because everyone believes in different-ness. We have been brought up like that. We have been taught to be so competitive - that I am different, that you are different. There is a culture of isolation and separation which has buried the Truth that we are One. So, it’s an uphill task to figure out.
author: Sri M

text: This is a beautiful world. It is complete in and of itself. There is no harm in giving and sharing love. But then, it becomes an obsession. When I become possessive about it, when I want it only for myself, the problem starts.
author: Sri M

text: To love your child or grandson is not a big deal. We are chemically built to do that. Even monkeys do. But if you love someone else’s child or grandchild, then that is something. But it is not easy. In spiritual life, things change as you evolve. You not only love what you think is yours but what others believe is theirs.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual growth happens at a different pace for different people. Everyone doesn’t have the same speed of growth, and you don’t have to imitate anyone.
author: Sri M

text: In the Guru Mantra, when we say ‘Sadgurum Tam Namaami’ we are not talking about any living being. We are talking about the Supreme Being. The real one is that which pervades everything everywhere and in the case of humans, may be able to connect to the divine within. The inner being is the real Guru.
author: Sri M

text: There is a state of mind of absolute calmness, where the mind remains absolutely still, quiet and calm like the full moon. It spreads its light everywhere, the cool light of the moon. That is the state which is potentially in all of us even though it may not be active. To contact that and to pay respects to that inner being is the most important part of Guru Purnima.
author: Sri M

text: The most important function of the Guru is to act as a well-polished mirror so that we see ourselves as we are, with all our imperfections.The teacher reflects what is going on in us. Sometimes this can be very unpleasant. A genuine spiritual teacher is not worried about the unpleasantness. When it gets very unpleasant, many people leave. What a teacher is looking for is not numbers but to see if one person can change. If we can change one person, that’s enough to change the world.
author: Sri M

text: You need to practise. The approach does not matter. Results come with constant practice. This helps you maintain your spiritual journey without disruption. It’s not the terminology that matters, it’s what you do.
author: Sri M

text: The ‘you do for me’ should go and be replaced with ‘I do for myself’. Practice! Your practice is your experience.
author: Sri M

text: We are all, in our true essence, free. But we have conditioned and hypnotized ourselves into this small little world we have created for ourselves. Can we get out of this? Can we see that the spark of the Divine also exists in each one of us?
author: Sri M

text: Bow to the deity in your own heart.
author: Sri M

text: The key principle of the teaching is that we are in our true essence complete and full. It’s because we haven’t recognized this that we are looking for it outside.
author: Sri M

text: Money is not everything. It can buy many things, but it cannot buy happiness or fulfillment.
author: Sri M

text: What is cancer? Simply put, it is when a group of cells forget how to stop multiplying. Our lives also become quite cancerous, as desires never end. But if that drive is channelized towards spiritual pursuit, then it’s not cancerous.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Upanishads, the person who is most intelligent will discover the limitations of one’s intellect.
author: Sri M

text: What is the need for Kriya? Kriya simply means - a technique, a method. A step-by-step way or method by which one learns to separate the mind from its distractions. Patanjali describes it as ‘Chitta Vritti Nirodha’.
author: Sri M

text: The aim of Kriya is how to make the mind that’s constantly engaged in the outside world go within and see.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya is a way to bring out the truth by practice – the truth that in the core of everyone’s consciousness, there is a spark of the divine.
author: Sri M

text: The practice of Kriya is to make the mind calm, sensitive, and free of distraction so that the divine is reflected in the ripple-less mirror of the mind, for real and not theoretically.
author: Sri M

text: People may think the Bhagavad Gita is merely philosophical talk. It’s not. It’s the most practical teaching which, apart from conveying the philosophy of life, also teaches one how to act, how to practice that by which one can find the divinity within.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever you do, you need to have a daily schedule. If you don’t, success is not possible because our minds have had a free run in various directions for all our lives. We need to retrieve and bring it back. It takes a long time for it to come back and move in one direction because the mind is distracted as a habit.
author: Sri M

text: The Yogi believes that the human body and mind are intimately linked, especially the brain, which in yogic texts is called the Sahasrara.
author: Sri M

text: The days are gone when people had to go sit in caves far away in the jungle for spiritual understanding and realization.
author: Sri M

text: We now need to look at how we can live in this world, which is quite nice. Living in this world, is it possible to be spiritual? If we don’t think of that, then there’s no point being spiritual.
author: Sri M

text: This life is a battlefield. Various forces, good and bad, are present and always opposing each other. In this battle of life, can we also touch the essence of our being and be spiritual? There’s no point in running away.
author: Sri M

text: We need jean-clad sanyasins. The paraphernalia should go and the reality should emerge.
author: Sri M

text: If somebody has no doubts, is innocent, simple-minded and had a movement towards the divine in one’s youth, this is so because they are already prepared. This is the case of someone who has done almost all of his or her sadhana and has returned to finish the remaining bit. Everybody cannot expect to do that.
author: Sri M

text: There are different ways to find the Truth. Follow whichever you prefer. The purpose of Kriya is to increase focus and speed.
author: Sri M

text: A Sthitaprajna is one whose state of mind has become balanced, steady, and unruffled, yet is still active. This is for the person living in this world, not in a cave far from everything.
author: Sri M

text: One who discovers through deep introspection that the Self is unruffled deep down has secured wisdom.
author: Sri M

text: When all the desires of heart have been understood and let go of, and when the spirit finds joy and satisfaction in itself without any external add-ons, then one is a person with steady wisdom.
author: Sri M

text: Running away from one’s circumstances is not the solution. When the mind is steady, the steadiness and wisdom are not dependent on external circumstances.
author: Sri M

text: Apart from material troubles, what we generally have are mind or ego problems. I think I am a wise man but when I go out, someone calls me a fool. What happens to my steady mind? It’s gone because I am dependent on my external conditions to maintain the steadiness.
author: Sri M

text: There is an eternal element in all of us that is joyous in its own nature.
author: Sri M

text: One day, there is an irresistible love for God, which you cannot explain. This happens because everybody’s brain is built for this.
author: Sri M

text: When you love, you don’t expect anything in return. Try to identify that as a divine emotion. Tell yourself that you will live like that without any external object.
author: Sri M

text: When the love for the Divine arises, it’s like an overflow. There are no questions.
author: Sri M

text: When you stop all reaching out, the Truth is. When you realize it’s here, then it is found.
author: Sri M

text: The human mind and the ego are intrinsically, by nature, conditioned and not infinite. You can move as close as you can to the Divine by removing these conditioning's as much as possible to make the mind pure. When you are that close to it, then it’s like the Sun. It burns you off. Then, you are not there.
author: Sri M

text: Whether on the path of self-realization or not, you should think that things will happen at the right time. Keep working; patience is of essence.
author: Sri M

text: Actually, it’s good to erase one’s yesterday and live today. You are lighter; there are no burdens.
author: Sri M

text: All who touch that which is called Moksha, Nirvana or Kaivalya, all of them know automatically at some point why they are here.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t go to extremes. If you go to one extreme in this world, you might get thrown to the other. Moderation is the key.
author: Sri M

text: The idea of looking within is to close one's eyes, look into the mind, and see how it's functioning. There are hundreds of thoughts in there. Can I keep observing them with the belief that, one day, I want these thoughts to cease? Then, there's a chance that I would get in touch with the core of my being.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not a passive state. It is a super-active state wherein there's action in the tranquility of mind, without agitation.
author: Sri M

text: When internal churning is on, that’s the time when you should not fall victim to it or get addicted to it. Instead, watch it, and it'll subside. Then, comes the 'Amrita' or nectar.
author: Sri M

text: We like to confine ourselves to the thought that we are puny little beings with our own interests, wandering here and there. But, in actuality, we are not.
author: Sri M

text: If the body has not rested and is not alert, then it cannot meditate. It'll impact the mind. So, keep your body in a state where it's not tortured by lack of sleep or extreme fasting.
author: Sri M

text: Human beings cannot exist without food and water in the 'Kaliyuga.' Of course, you can practice moderation. The body should've enough nourishment. But, all in moderation.
author: Sri M

text: Moderation in all areas - eating, drinking, sleeping, and also entertainment. It takes your mind off its constant work. But don’t make entertainment your sole aim in life.
author: Sri M

text: Once the mind becomes disciplined, then it can be established solely on the inner Self. Then, it is free from the longing for other things. Only then, you are free.
author: Sri M

text: The mind of a yogi becomes like the flame of a lamp that does not flicker.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t think that there aren’t difficulties in a Yogi’s life; surely there are. But, the Yogi is not affected by it. He is free. He wants other people also not to be affected by it.
author: Sri M

text: One of the biggest problems we face when we sit down to meditate is distraction. If we don’t fix a daily schedule, success is not possible. The mind, out of habit, runs in various directions; you should be able to catch and fix it.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is distracted continuously because, for most people, the prana (vital energy) is working through the ida (left channel) and the pingala (right channel), which are meant for worldly things.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya aims to direct the energies (prana) operating in the left and right channels (ida and pingala) to the sushumna (central channel). Once this process is underway, then your distractions become less.
author: Sri M

text: Once you are an expert, you can sit and halt your distractions in a matter of minutes. There is thought, but no distraction. There is energy, but no unrestricted use of it. There is attention, but it's single-pointed. There is joy, but only inner joy. There is entertainment, but it's the entertainment of the snake. You are the snake charmer.
author: Sri M

text: Most of the time, in the ordinary course of our lives, we are dependent on external things for happiness. Looking inside means to sit once in a while, close your eyes, and go into your mind to see how it is functioning.
author: Sri M

text: If you look at life, it's in itself a miracle. You don’t need any external miracles.
author: Sri M

text: What we cannot explain, we call a miracle. Usually, miracles happen due to laws of nature that most people don’t know of. All the Yogi does is to tap these laws, so that he/she can operate it.
author: Sri M

text: It's dangerous for sadhaks (spiritual aspirants) to get caught up in miracles. Most of the miracles are of this world, and if you get caught up in it, you're also caught up in this world.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest miracle for a great yogi is to guide someone to the highest. If one person in a million reaches that, it's a great miracle.
author: Sri M

text: It doesn’t matter who the teacher is, what he or she looks like, etc. What's important is the wisdom that comes from the teacher.
author: Sri M

text: Like the frog that lives on earth and water, the one who has understood the Truth, whose mind is anchored to the Spirit, can live in this world also.
author: Sri M

text: If we live in this world with the heart anchored to the core Truth, then we can live more efficiently than ever before.
author: Sri M

text: OM represents the sound by which that primordial creation starts and ends.
author: Sri M

text: OM is the bridge that links this world to the other.
author: Sri M

text: Unless something dies and disappears, there's no place for anything new to take birth.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual seeker is not tempted by anything other than to find the truth one-pointedly.
author: Sri M

text: Your real essence is not born and does not die. The ‘I”, which is witness to all states of existence,does not get involved or get destroyed.
author: Sri M

text: Use your mind as the bow, your will as the bowstring and ‘OM’ as the arrow. Aim at the Supreme Being and let go of the arrow one-pointedly.
author: Sri M

text: Is there some way by which the ordinary mind, caught up in this world with its pains and pleasures, can be free and touch the essence? The study of this is called the Brahmavidya, and the way to do this is called Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not merely standing on your head. It’s much more. The true meaning of Yoga is the complete ending of the mind's distractions.
author: Sri M

text: If one can stop the distractions of the mind-stuff, then the mind in its tranquil state reflects the reality of one’s true being.
author: Sri M

text: All meditations essentially boil down to how to make the mind free of distractions, how to make it settle down, and finally how to remain in the eye of the storm, be completely free and not be distracted by anything.
author: Sri M

text: Only a relaxed mind can have one-pointed attention.
author: Sri M

text: There are many types of Yoga. There is the yoga that you practice, Patanjali’s Yoga. There is the Karma Yoga, which is about doing good work continuously, a self-less action until you are purified. Another way is by devotion or Bhakti Yoga. There are ways and means to open your heart. The other way is to inquire about the true reality - Who am I?
author: Sri M

text: Some people say that they can’t sit in meditation. So, what to do? Do good work for others. Slowly, the mind gets purified enough to attempt Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is so limited that it cannot find the Reality through thought. So, what do you do? Open the heart.
author: Sri M

text: The world around causes pain in various ways. Of course, there are little moments of happiness, but they are all temporary. While living in this world, can we understand that we are passing through something that's painful at times, and is something we need to leave at some point? Is there something that's permanent in the midst of it all?
author: Sri M

text: Forget all the past that has happened and look at the present, so that the future is good.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation is the capacity that one develops through practice to be one-pointed and to continue naturally in that state until what one is meditating upon is the only thing that remains. You even forget the fact that you are present.
author: Sri M

text: One-pointed attention is the most critical thing in meditation. And that one-pointedness opens up the pathway to that which is One.
author: Sri M

text: When you become more mindful of yourself, you become more mindful of the outer world.
author: Sri M

text: People don’t realize the power of harmful thoughts. So, while you expand your mind, keep your mind in goodness.
author: Sri M

text: If you are too attached only to the biological module of a family, then your mind cannot expand to the universal. No mind can live without any attachment. So, we move from a lower attachment to a higher one.
author: Sri M

text: If you have kissed the garment of Truth, then you see the universal in even the mundane. You see the heart; you don’t see anything else.
author: Sri M

text: A prayer from ancient times that is eternally relevant: May the whole world be happy, may we see all that is auspicious, may nobody suffer.
author: Sri M

text: Bow down to the Supreme Teacher, who is beyond the understanding of the ordinary mind. Of course, one understands it when the mind is not just ordinary, but slightly above it.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is to prepare to the mind towards the extraordinary. And, perhaps then, it gets a glimpse of the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: In the wisdom teachings of all ancient religions, there is no intrinsic core difference. It is the same.
author: Sri M

text: There was a man called Adi Shankaracharya who walked across India and established centers and ashrams . One of his theories was that no rituals or external factors could take one to the Supreme Truth. One needs ‘Viveka’ (discrimination) and ‘Vairagya’ ( non-possessiveness ).
author: Sri M

text: One of Adi Shankaracharya’s main theories was that rituals are excellent for a specific purpose, but won’t lead you to the Supreme Truth.
author: Sri M

text: Without Viveka (discrimination) and Vairagya (non-possessiveness), you can have yogic powers, but you won’t touch the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: The search for Nirvana (as in Buddhism) and the search for Moksha (as in Vedanta) are not different things. The core is no different; both are the ultimate freedom.
author: Sri M

text: In the Yoga Sutras, Patanjali uses the word Kaivalya for the Ultimate Reality, which means ‘only or alone’. A person who has touched Kaivalya is kind of alone in the sense that there is nothing left except the core of one’s existence. There is only That.
author: Sri M

text: Satsang is a group of people trying to find the Truth. You and I are going to look at the problem together.
author: Sri M

text: Dialogue, not argument, is critical between the teacher and student. The Bhagavad Gita is a dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna. Krishna tells Arjuna that his mind should be like a flame when there is no wind.
author: Sri M

text: When we get to a position where we have money or power, we forget that the source is somewhere else. Then we get so proud that we try to challenge the source from where prosperity comes. And, that’s the end of it.
author: Sri M

text: There is no difference in the ancient universal teachings. But when it becomes more organized, it loses its core. Why? Because you get more interested in the external aspects.
author: Sri M

text: There is a fountain of happiness inside us waiting to be discovered. And, one shot is enough; it’s better than Tequila!
author: Sri M

text: In Mundaka Upanishad, Mundaka means shaven-headed. So, it’s intended for Renunciants who have shaven off their hair. It indicates people who have cleared all their negativities and ego—somebody who is free from all that.
author: Sri M

text: The highest knowledge is that which leads you to the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: Some people have so much theoretical knowledge and are swollen with the ego of this knowledge that they begin to think they are spiritually illuminated and start teaching people. When they do that, it’s like the blind leading the blind.
author: Sri M

text: The theoretical aspect is one thing, and experience is another. Some people understand this Truth and become totally silent because it can’t be expressed in words.
author: Sri M

text: When all supports fail, then there is that—the Ultimate support.
author: Sri M

text: Dharana (concentration) is equivalent to relaxation. The mind flows naturally towards something without barriers. It is the capacity or the effort involved in fixing one’s attention on an image, or a symbol, or a sound, or an idea.
author: Sri M

text: There is one element that links you to thought (which has no language), and that is music. Music is an excellent help for meditation because it takes you away from the conditionings of language. Music is uniting, as opposed to the language that is sometimes dividing.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t think that meditation happens only when you sit cross-legged in one place. Meditation is any activity that brings about love, affection, the calmness of mind, and tranquility leading to the ultimate goal.
author: Sri M

text: From the science of Yoga, we understand that in every human being, there are many channels in the body through which Prana or life energy flows.
author: Sri M

text: Ahimsa is an attitude of not causing injury to any living being, including human beings. Some people feed sugar to ants, but they have no problem pulling someone down when they go home.
author: Sri M

text: Devotion is required to move on the spiritual path, besides a rough understanding of what we are doing and why we are doing it.
author: Sri M

text: Being truthful and honest is a prerequisite for any spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: Truth is infinite. So, there must be infinite ways of approaching it. Truth is like the sun; there is nothing secret about it. It is open to all, especially now when the human brain has evolved enough to look at it accurately. No more rahasyas – secrets, move away now!
author: Sri M

text: If I can go there and touch it, you can also do it. It may take time, but you will hit upon it one day.
author: Sri M

text: When you understand that the spiritual journey is not something dry but exciting and if you are genuinely interested in it, then you will have no distractions whatsoever. Until then, you have to keep bringing back your distracted mind to the journey. Keep doing it till the mind is trained not to be distracted until you enjoy That, and there are no more distractions.
author: Sri M

text: If you can’t keep your toilet clean, how will you keep your mind clean?
author: Sri M

text: The best way to deal with ego is to gradually and repeatedly understand that you are the actual problem. If you can deal with it, then you can deal with anything.
author: Sri M

text: First, we need to develop a relationship with the ego. Unless and until we can look at it thoroughly, we will not be able to study that facet of the ego, which needs to be dealt with.
author: Sri M

text: A teacher wants to help bring about a change in the student and would like to understand the student completely before instructing, but the student doesn’t want to let some parts of the mind be available to the teacher to study. So, he or she keeps it shut under lock and key. How can the teacher study it then? If it’s not studied, then how does one deal with it?
author: Sri M

text: The real meaning of Karma Yoga is to work—not for oneself but for others, and not expecting results every minute. You must apply your mind to work on a long-term basis.
author: Sri M

text: An example of Karma Yoga is looking after someone who is not well, as you get nothing out of it. This act is Karma Yoga in its purest form.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever happens, even if you are sick, try not to miss the routine practice of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: The moment you become stressed, you cannot do your work. So, try to work without stress deliberately. You’ll be able to do better, and your mind expands. You will begin to touch things that you usually cannot. Giving attention to something is not stressful.
author: Sri M

text: Concentration, according to Yoga, is the same thing as relaxation.
author: Sri M

text: If you feel that you are being led on the spiritual journey for spiritual progress and that person is able to help you, then that is your Guru.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot go looking for a Guru with a magnifying glass; you may not find one anywhere. If you find that someone is not trying to take over your mind, but instead allowing you the freedom to figure out how to handle your mind, then perhaps that is your teacher. Is he interested in helping you or taking help from you?
author: Sri M

text: Who will give? Only those who are full. Fullness is also called emptiness—Poorna is also Shunya.
author: Sri M

text: Try to find a teacher whose only interest is in your development. When you do, watch the person in all circumstances. And, if you find that his or her interest is in you and not himself, then you have come upon someone who might be able to help you out.
author: Sri M

text: When you touch that, it’s not as if you are completely cut off from the world or that you can’t function in the world. You can actually function better because the source of your intelligence from where your intellect comes is expanded. The cells of your brain and body have changed. But the catch is, to touch that, you might have to withdraw for some time.
author: Sri M

text: If you’ve touched That, the world will still go on. You can still contribute, and you’ll probably do it in a better way, in a calm, peaceful and quiet way.
author: Sri M

text: When you are starting on the journey you do need some time and solitude. Because in the middle of the world, it’s not so easy. But, once you are stabilized, then you can function and not only in a small way.
author: Sri M

text: The next stage of evolution is the spiritual evolution, from Homo Sapien to Yogi.
author: Sri M

text: You give up your individuality for yourself.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t take the teacher’s form so seriously, but listen to the words and figure out if you can find it yourself. If you make the personality more important and worship the personality you may get stuck. The teaching does not depend on anyone person. The teaching is Universal.
author: Sri M

text: Vairagya from the Vedantic point of view is that you discriminate what is real and what is unreal.
author: Sri M

text: If more people wake up, then there is a solution for the suffering.
author: Sri M

text: Usually, the mind is scattered, therefore your energies are also scattered. To find out that which is important, you need to gather these energies. Therefore, all the training of various schools is to make a mold in which this shapeless thing can be stuffed inside and made into a certain shape. Once you’ve done that, then you break the mold.
author: Sri M

text: The Bindu is the sum total of your individual existence or Shakti, the dynamic self. As it ascends to higher levels of awareness, this Bindu loses its conditioning and then becomes one with Shivam. It realizes its intrinsic nature as Shivam. For that, the muck has to go from the sushumna. This is the practice.
author: Sri M

text: We all survive, exist and live because there is joy, not because there is suffering. But, suffering is inevitable when you enjoy. There are two sides always. There cannot be only suffering or only joy, it depends on the person who has gone through it.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Upanishads, creation is an evolution of the Spirit that goes into the matter and then when you realize it is Spirit, it returns to its essence. And, very often suffering is the anvil on which it is shaped properly.
author: Sri M

text: When all things have subsided in the brain, only then will we know the true nature of the mind. And that mind doesn’t need grace. That mind is grace itself.
author: Sri M

text: Fortunately, anybody who has touched it feels that it is like a circle with its circumference everywhere and center nowhere. Even the word ‘vast’ cannot define it. Everything must go.
author: Sri M

text: The more a person goes into the depths of spiritual understanding and meditation, the person becomes more humble.
author: Sri M

text: If I say I know everything, then the mind is closed. When the mind becomes closed, humility slowly vanishes.
author: Sri M

text: You may know some things and have the capacity to know many things if you want. But certainly, there are other people who also know things which you don’t know of.
author: Sri M

text: Grace cannot come unless we have some kind of humility. The moment it’s gone then you shut the doors and they are concrete doors, not ordinary wooden doors. So even if Grace wants to come, it cannot penetrate.
author: Sri M

text: Grace is like a beautiful breeze when it blows. It carries its own beautiful scents of the flowers that it blows through. It’s available to us, but how will we get the breeze if we shut our windows and doors? All sadhana is only to help us learn how to open them.
author: Sri M

text: The first thing you realize is that you are nothing. We are insignificant little particles of sand near the sea. We come and we are gone tomorrow. Humility is an inner feeling that ‘I am nothing in this vast world’. The Great Ones know this.
author: Sri M

text: What you know, your scholarship and your practice that is one side. That your mind absorbs that and blooms is because of truthfulness, non-injury to others and humility.
author: Sri M

text: Nobody has moved on the spiritual path only by reading or by collecting material. You cannot attain the highest; Nirvana, Moksha or Kaivalya by standing on your head for three hours.
author: Sri M

text: There is one important requisite to find the truth, whichever path you may follow. And that is the urgent, earnest desire to find the truth.
author: Sri M

text: The first requisite is seriousness and urgency for finding the Truth. Then, the way you go depends on your personality, your background, and your past. So, before you accept a path, don’t be in a hurry.
author: Sri M

text: A true spiritual teacher is not in the business of gathering disciples. A teacher is one that is more concerned about the aspirants’ aspirations and that he/she should move towards the Truth, rather than wanting them to be a follower.
author: Sri M

text: Among the Sufis, if you go to a person, he will train you, then after a while, he will say that you have learned all that you can from me, go to the other one. So you learn. Finally, you come to the one who is your final teacher.
author: Sri M

text: The meaning of the word meditation is basically, to contemplate.
author: Sri M

text: Shunya is not nothing. It is that from which this entire universe has come, and into which it has to go back. Actually, one cannot define something which is so abstract to nothing. Actually it means no-thing. Then what it is, only one who knows, knows.
author: Sri M

text: From the Vedantic point of view to the Upanishads to the teachings of Nath sampradaya and the practice of Yoga, there are innumerable links with the Buddhist system. It doesn’t matter what you call the ultimate thing. You may call it Nirvana. In Vedantic terms you may call it Moksha, in Yogic terms, you may call it Kaivalya.
author: Sri M

text: Kaivalya is derived from the word ‘Kevala’ - only. In Kaivalya the Yogi understands that there is only ‘One’. Unity in diversity where Prakriti is completely overcome. There is only the Purusha, like the supreme Brahman.
author: Sri M

text: The inquiry into what you really are begins with the understanding that this body doesn’t exist for long, it dies. So, when I die, do I die with the body? Or am I still around? If I’m still around and if I have a personality and a subtle body, still it is mine and I’m still me. So if all these are mine, then I must be different than mine. One day, in the quietness of the inquiry, perhaps it will dawn on you what you actually are.
author: Sri M

text: Very few people are interested in finding the true identity. That’s OK. Finally, you have to come back to your source.
author: Sri M

text: It doesn’t matter what your belief is. If you need to survive in this world, you need to put in hard work.
author: Sri M

text: Once the thought has entered that one has to do prayas, you can be rest assured that the Kripa (grace) is already there. So put your mind on the Prayas (effort).
author: Sri M

text: There are millions of people on this earth, right? Why is it that only some people want to look for spiritual matters and others don’t want to? That means a little bit of Kripa (grace) is already there. If that is not there, then you cannot even go into it.
author: Sri M

text: The Bhagavad Gita is one of the earliest textbooks of spiritual understanding and exploration which says that there are innumerable ways towards the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot simply sit down and meditate without understanding what meditation is, even if you know the technique.
author: Sri M

text: All our thought processes are made up of language. Music is something which cuts across all barriers.
author: Sri M

text: The pure teaching of Krishna is beyond words, but Vyasa has no way other than using words. If I don’t use words, how can I talk to you? But also understand that words are limited and there are limitations in words.
author: Sri M

text: The actual aim of understanding the Gita is to go beyond all construction, all words, all conditioning until the Supreme Brahman is face to face with you.
author: Sri M

text: We all have a set of duties, but to perform those duties not worrying too much about the ultimate result whether it is good or bad. It is nice to think that it should be good, but even if it becomes bad, one shouldn’t fall into a depression. Stand back and think where we went wrong and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: Sanyasa is not for the lazy. A true sanyasin is one who lives in this world and acts without worrying too much about the results of the action.
author: Sri M

text: According to Sankya, everything in life, material as well of the human mind is made up of three gunas. Sattva, Rajas, Tamas. Every human being has these three in some percentage.
author: Sri M

text: What is true Sanyasa? You can wear jeans and still be a true sanyasin. How? If you can work and not worry about the fruits. If your aim is to shift from tamo guna to rajo guna to sattva guna, then, you don’t have to change any external circumstances. You can meditate, you can reach Moksha.
author: Sri M

text: If you work surrendering the fruits of your actions to the Lord, then, such a person is working, but doing detached work. Such a person quickly moves towards the path of meditation because the mind becomes quiet. It is not work that is disturbing your mind, it’s the expectation that is disturbing your mind.
author: Sri M
